name: John Whitmer
role: Scribe and first appointed Church historian
dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, appointed Church historian in March 1831, and excommunicated at Far West in March 1838.
importance: Section 15 answers his wish to know what would be most worth to him in June 1829. He served as a scribe and copied revelations for Joseph Smith. Section 47 names him to keep a regular history, and section 69 sends him to Missouri with the revelations and Oliver Cowdery. Section 70 makes him a steward over the revelations.
connections: He was a son of Peter Whitmer Sr. and a brother of David and Peter Whitmer Jr. Section 30 sends him to preach near the home of Philip Burroughs.

sources.title: John Whitmer, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 27 Aug. 1802, Pennsylvania; died 11 July 1878 at the Far West site; one of the Eight Witnesses; historian c. 8 Mar. 1831; assistant in the Missouri presidency 1834; excommunicated 10 Mar. 1838. Bare “John” not listed as ambiguous; sections 15, 26, 30 address him that way.
